page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ce4.xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon E5-2667 v4 processor running at 3.2 GHz. It features 4 physical cores with 1 thread per core, providing 4 dedicated vCPUs. The instance is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the ecs.ce4.xlarge delivers modest processing capabilities. In stress-ng testing, both single-core and multi-core CPU performance fall into the bottom 25% tier. Similarly, Geekbench multi-core scores and Passmark CPU metrics reflect lower-tier performance, though single-core Geekbench and single-threaded gzip compression tests reach average levels. Memory bandwidth is a notable bottleneck, with large-block read operations registering in the bottom 10% at 22.44 GB/sec, and write operations remaining weak.

Given its hardware profile, the ecs.ce4.xlarge is best suited for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high-performance compute or rapid storage I/O. Appropriate use cases include caching layers, lightweight database operations, and basic web serving. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the use of legacy Intel Xeon E5 v4 architecture positions this instance as a budget-friendly option for applications requiring a high RAM-to-vCPU ratio without the premium cost of modern CPU generations.
